title: Playing old tunes for her at home on his troubled clarinet
summary: In his final week he played long-forgotten compositions for her in the back room while struggling with clarinet repairs.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: fallen or the children got hold of it. I don't know what happened but he was having an awful lot of trouble with it. And I can remember in the back room many times he'd lay there trying to fix it himself and do the repair shop and it wasn't fixed to his liking. And we'd try to fix it and cork it up and pad it up and bend the keys and so forth. And he'd run through. I do remember though the past week prior to his death, before going into the hospital, he had played many compositions he had never played in years. He was playing for me that I hadn't been familiar with. And he says, too bad that we had never gotten together to play with the musicians that they can't remember some of these tunes. And he'd run them over and somehow I couldn't even remember them now. But they were beautiful and he'd play them for me. And he'd ask me if I knew them or if I remember. It was like a guessing game.
But he played in the back? Mm-hmm. In the back. Yeah.

He played more or less for me, I think, because he knew how much I enjoyed listening to him. And he'd lie there and he'd just lie on the bed with his feet up and he'd play with his clarinet and he'd say, well, do you remember this one or do you know this one? He was quite surprised that I knew as many as I did.
